subject.title: [Bug] Telegram exec approval bubble not dismissed after clicking approve

question: Should maintainers close or adopt the open conflicting fork PR before allowing a fresh narrow fix for this issue?
rationale: The remaining bug is narrow, but the issue is linked to an open closing PR from a fork that is conflicting and targets the removed handler path; automation should not create a competing fix until maintainers decide how to handle that candidate.

options.title: Close or supersede the fork PR
options.body: Close the conflicting fork PR as obsolete or superseded, then let a narrow replacement target `extensions/telegram/src/approval-handler.runtime.ts` with live Telegram proof.

options.title: Adopt and rewrite the fork PR
options.body: Have a maintainer take over the fork branch only if they intend to replace the obsolete handler diff with the active-runtime fix shape.

options.title: Keep waiting on the fork PR
options.body: Leave this issue blocked on the fork PR, accepting that the current linked branch is stale, conflicting, and not a clean landing candidate.

recommendation.title: Close or supersede the fork PR
recommendation.body: Close the conflicting fork PR as obsolete or superseded, then let a narrow replacement target `extensions/telegram/src/approval-handler.runtime.ts` with live Telegram proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The native approval lifecycle refactor history makes this the best available routing owner for the handler/runtime boundary decision.
